rules.title: User logs
rules.removes: Log files apps write to your Library's Logs folder, including crash reports.
rules.notes: Includes DiagnosticReports. TidyMyMac's log folder is on the protected floor.
evidence: Logs in ~/Library/Logs are diagnostic text written by apps and the system; apps don't read them back to work (observed, macOS 26.7.1).

rules.title: System logs
rules.removes: Log files apps and services write to the computer-wide Library's Logs folder.
rules.keeps: The unified system log, Apple's diagnostic store and TidyMyMac's own helper log.
evidence: Files in /Library/Logs are plain-text diagnostics; apps and macOS create them again as needed (observed, macOS 26.7.1).

rules.title: Old system log archives
rules.removes: Compressed and numbered old copies of system logs in /private/var/log.
rules.keeps: The current log files and the unified log store.
rules.notes: Only rotated archives (.gz, .bz2, .xz or a trailing number); the helper's zone enforces this.
evidence: newsyslog rotates these archives and never reads them back (man newsyslog).
